description: Verify that DUT drops a non-gratuitous ARP Response addressed to someone else (target_ip ≠ DUT IP) and re-resolves on next egress — addressing-target variant of ARP_22/28
approach:
[Objective]
Unsolicited Replies addressed at another peer must not seed DUT's cache. This is the receive-time analogue of 'don't accept information you weren't asked about'. Phase 2 forces an egress that exercises whatever DUT did or did not learn from phase 1.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Response injected
   • opcode      = 2
   • target_ip   = some other peer's IP (NOT DUT)   ← key: not addressed to DUT
   • sender_ip   = HOST-1-IP / sender_mac = MAC-ADDR1

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup
   ⇒ stimulates DUT to send a UDP response to HOST-1-IP.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request for HOST-1-IP
   • DUT's UDP must not use MAC-ADDR1 as eth_dst

[Pass condition]
DUT emits its own ARP Request for HOST-1-IP and does not use MAC-ADDR1.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_udp_used_injected_mac — DUT used MAC-ADDR1 → it learned from a Reply not addressed to it
• Fail_no_dut_arp_request — DUT did not resolve via its own Request

verdicts.Pass: DUT dropped the cross-addressed Reply and resolved via its own Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_udp_used_injected_mac: DUT used MAC-ADDR1 — learned from a Reply addressed to someone else
verdicts.Fail_no_dut_arp_request: DUT did not resolve via its own Request — reception path incomplete
